source.title: Unlearning Under Imbalance: Benchmarking Fairness in Multimodal LLM Unlearning
source.authors: L. Orsingher; Thomas De Min; Massimiliano Mancini; Davide Talon; Elisa Ricci

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present. Some table formatting is flattened, but the selected EM values can be assigned to methods and models from the layout.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates the effect of several unlearning methods on targeted-knowledge accuracy and retained performance in a new multimodal benchmark, but does not test the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports unlearning outcomes for baseline methods and FAUN, including forget-set exact match and retain-set exact match. It does not apply fine-tuning recovery attacks, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompting attacks. Its discussions of inference-time steering and cited prior work are not additional experimental results for those attacks.
record.test_reason: A new setting: multimodal fictitious-identity VQA (FAIRGET) with unbalanced forget sets. It reports forget and retain exact match for eight baseline methods and FAUN against original and retrained references, which bears on the first part of A (forgetting to the retrained/chance level while keeping ability). No recovery attack of any kind is run (no relearning, ablation, quantization or adversarial prompting), so B–F are untested. Evaluation already uses rephrased questions on held-out images, but there is no unrephrased comparison, so it cannot show recovery.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude FAUN gives the best trade-off between forgetting, retained utility and fairness (lowest DP), and call its weight updates 'permanent' unlearning. They draw no conclusions about recovery attacks. They also note all methods degrade general VQA utility (MME) because the retain set is FAIRGET-only.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates unlearning methods on a newly constructed multimodal fictitious-identity VQA benchmark with unbalanced forget sets. It is not a reproduction of the recovery-attack procedures in the original sources; FAUN adds activation steering and bias-informed PCA.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary by model, forgotten group, and unlearning ratio. The selected rows use a 50% single-group forget setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Unbalanced forget sets shift demographic parity on unseen identities (e.g. SimNPO DP 25.19 on Idefics right-wing); bias-informed PCA reduces it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning skewed toward one demographic group introduces bias in predictions about unseen people.

record.problems: No recovery attacks are run, so the study cannot establish whether forgotten information can be recovered or whether unlearning only hides it. A chance-level accuracy reference is not reported; the stated reference is a retrained model without the forget data. No uncertainty estimates are shown for the reported table results.
record.rows_left_out: To stay within 60 rows, Table 2 and Table 3 retain-set EM rows for MIU, IDK, and FTTP are omitted; their forget EM results are included. Also omitted are results from the ratio sweep (Fig. 4 and Table 8), multi-group unlearning (Fig. 6), FIUBench (Table 4), additional group/model tables (Tables 6-7), ablations (Fig. 5), and MME utility (Table 5). These are reported for fairness, benchmark or method comparisons rather than recovery attacks; the selected FAIRGET results cover the main method/model/group outcomes for V1.

untested.parts: That simple attacks don't recover the knowledge: no attack is run. FAUN's 'permanent' unlearning claim is asserted, not attack-tested.
All: no relearning or fine-tuning after unlearning.
All: no direction ablation and no deletion-vs-suppression analysis. FAUN uses steering as a training signal, not as an attack.
All: no jailbreak, language or in-context attack. Rephrased test questions are the default eval, with no unrephrased baseline.
All: FAUN is not evaluated against any recovery attack.

missing.what: Forget-set normalized probability of the correct answer stays near the original after unlearning (e.g. FAUN 0.411, SimNPO 0.419 vs original 0.480, retrained 0.270). This is residual likelihood despite the EM drop, bearing on whether knowledge is removed.
MIA AUC after unlearning (about 52–56) stays near the original (52) rather than the retrained model (63–65). Forget samples remain statistically unlike a retrained model.
Retain EM for MIU, IDK and FTTP is needed to judge the cost behind F1/F10/F13 (e.g. IDK low net-worth retain 16.63, MIU about 68). Declared omitted, but it is needed for verdicts.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's blanket 'challenges' for most rows was relabelled: part-way forgetting is partial, so limits_scope; only LUNAR-Idefics shows absent forgetting. The retrained model (about 17% forget EM) is the effective chance reference. Table 5 (MME) shows large general-utility drops for all methods (MME-C 671.8 to 246–486); it is declared omitted but relevant to A's 'keeps general ability'. Forget-prob and MIA results hint at residual knowledge but are not recovery tests.

versions.untested_parts: No recovery attacks are tested. The paper does not report a chance-level reference; retrained models without the forget data serve as the stated gold-standard comparison.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning-set recovery attack.
No ablation of an activation direction to recover knowledge. The paper describes inference-time steering as temporary, but does not test recovery by internal edits.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery attack.
FAUN is presented as a fairness-aware unlearning method, but the paper does not test whether it resists the recovery attacks listed in the claim.

source_check.notes: Tables are flattened but cells place by method order; all values verified against Tables 2-3. Only the forget/retain part of A is tested (no recovery attacks). FAUN rows (F9, F18, F27) are the study's own method. Not in rows: Table 5 MME drop (MME-C 671.8 to 246.4-485.7 for GAD/RL/SimNPO/FAUN) and appendix groups (Tables 6-7), which show the same pattern.

statements.correction: Qwen2.5-VL-7B, FAIRGET, man with right-wing orientation, 50% forget: MIU forget EM 16.93 vs retrained 17.20 (original 74.91); retain EM 68.09 vs original 67.24. MIU uses group annotations (privileged baseline). No recovery attacks; test questions are rephrasings on held-out images. No numeric chance level; the retrained model is the reference. Other methods reach forget EM about 27-63 on Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Idefics3-8B.
statements.problem: Gives no facts for this study, yet cites its F1 under A support among studies tested with prompt, paraphrase and sampling attacks. This study runs no recovery attacks, so it bears only on the forget/retain part of A. F1 is MIU, a privileged baseline that uses group labels; most other methods forget only part-way.
